notes.title: Remove camera jump when you left-click on a tile.
notes.content: This patch removes the left-click-to-jump-camera interaction, because A) no one was using it, B) it's kind of superfluous now that we have click-to-drag, and C) it was the cause of a bunch of weird "why is the camera jumping around?" issues.

notes.title: Update 1.3
notes.content: [p]This update is kind of a strange one: it's sort of a major update, because it adds a [b]whole new scenario[/b] that's unlocked right from the start. But it's sort of a minor update, because that scenario is a free-form [b]Sandbox mode[/b] where it's impossible to win (or lose!), but you can build freely and explore. [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45530603/13d4f52ae3d180fbd527887eaba5432f06163563.jpg"][/img][/p][p]I'm not a big "sandbox" kind of player myself, but even I lost a few more hours than I'd care to admit just chilling out and building a giant island without having to worry about mana. If that's your thing – if you just want to plop tiles for a bit and relax – this update is for you![/p]

notes.title: Update 1.2
notes.content: [p]🖱️ Mouse-only players, this one's for you! The big change in this update is the addition of a new camera movement mode: right-click-and-drag with the mouse now rotates, zooms, and tilts the camera – allowing you to move freely (and, really, play the whole game) with just the mouse.[/p][p]I've also added a few bonus quality-of-life features folks have asked for, like an in-game UI scale slider, and added a highlight outline that shows you the current selected tile. If you're playing on a smaller screen (cough Steam Deck cough) this one will probably make your island-building a lot less error-prone. I'm pretty much a 100% Steam Deck player myself, and I'm definitely a fan.[/p][p]Hopefully you will be, too.[/p][list][*][p]Fixed a bug where corner ribbons on foil cards did not disappear on hover (in the card library and when selecting cards to draw).[/p][/*][*][p]Extended loading screen tips so they stay on-screen long enough to actually read.[/p][/*][*][p]Right click-and-drag with the mouse now rotates and zooms the camera. [/p][/*][*][p]Added a UI scale slider right inline in the in-game menu.[/p][/*][*][p]Added a white outline to land tiles when they’re hovered or selected.[/p][/*][*][p]Made the “this card can’t be played on this tile” indicator (a red X-marks-the-spot) larger and more prominent.[/p][/*][/list][p]I'm still working on the card balance for the first big (free!) content update coming in a few weeks, but until then keep those bug reports and feature requests coming! Best place is probably to leave 'em in the comments to this post or in a review.[/p]

notes.title: Update 1.1, plus the BIG Fall Showcase
notes.content: [p]🏝️ Hey, fellow island folks! I've gotten some great feedback and a bunch of [i]fantastic[/i] suggestions for improvements and new content in this past week following the launch, and I'm pleased to say that I'm releasing an update to [i]Isles & Tiles[/i] today that fixes a handful of bugs and makes a few tweaks here and there that should make the game a fair bit nicer to play.[/p][p]Big thanks in particular to [b]Renraku [/b]for a fantastic Steam review that included a veritable laundry list of great suggestions and quality bug reports. A lot of those have been fixed in this update, and I hope to have more to come next week![/p][list][*][p]Fix incorrect description on Blacksmith card, to indicate that it produces +1 iron for every 2 (not 1) adjacent mines[/p][/*][*][p]Fix one-time mana bonus from playing a Mana resource card (was 5, now 10) so it matches the description on the card.[/p][/*][*][p]Tweaked the size & auto-scaling of the current hand, so it displays slightly smaller  and adapts better to hands with 8+ cards.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a bug where Rune cards would still appear in your draw pile even when ‘toggled off’ in the card library.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a localization bug in Japanese & Chinese where the “Skip for N Gold” button could sometimes have missing glyphs.[/p][/*][*][p]The corner ribbons on foil cards now fade out when you hover the card, to prevent them from obscuring which tile types a card can be played on. [/p][/*][/list][p]And finally, [i]Isles & Tiles[/i] is part of the [url="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BQ3rDpbvxIg"]Best Indie Games Fall Showcase[/url], taking place on September 2nd. Be sure to check it out, as I'm sure there will be a [i]smorgasbord[/i] of awesome indie games on display![/p]

notes.title: Back to School Celebration
notes.content: [p]Need one last blast of that chill summer feeling before school starts? Check out [i]Isles & Tiles[/i], out now and on sale for 15% off during the 2025 Back to School Games Celebration.[/p]

notes.title: Prerelease Update 3
notes.content: [p]So, a confession: development on the (free!) post-release content update for [i]Isles & Tiles[/i] has been a bit slower for the last month or two than I'd planned. That's 100% because I finally got my hands on an OLED Steam Deck in order to make sure the game plays well on the it, and [b]wow[/b] is this thing an absolute rockstar of a machine. I'm kind of in love.[/p][p][/p][p](It didn't help that the Deck arrived pretty much the same time as the [i]Oblivion[/i] remaster; I'm such a sucker for a good nostalgia trip, and stomping around Cyrodil on the Steam Deck was such a delight).[/p][p][/p][p]Anyway, all that's to say that the last pre-release update for [i]Isles & Tiles [/i]is here, and mostly fixes a bunch of little edge-case UI bugs that made the game less nice to play on tiny screens like the Deck. So if you're looking for a chill game to add to your Steam Deck, you can safely ignore the "Steam is still learning about this game" warning – [i]Isles & Tiles[/i] plays [b]great[/b] on the Deck, and it's now my primary testing device.[/p]

notes.title: Prerelease Update 2
notes.content: [p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45530603/fc7e123683099c1bd857846ec85558854e89d2f4.jpg"][/img][/p][p]It turns out that a [i]lot[/i] more folks are playing on Steam Deck than I would have expected! I'm still working on proper Steam Deck support which I expect to have done by the end of this weekend (sorry, new Next Fest Steam Deck players!), but in the meantime I've updated both the game and the demo to use a custom, nicer UI scale on the Steam Deck's relatively small native screen resolution. [i]Isles & Tiles[/i] will also ship with a custom Steam Deck input template – look for it on the Workshop if it doesn't show up by default![/p][p]There's no other new content in this update, sadly. I have a ton more story beats and decisions coming in the next update, but I'm not quite happy with some of 'em so you'll have to wait until next week to check those out.[/p]

notes.title: Prerelease Update 1
notes.content:
Happy Isles & Demos! Based on some early feedback, I've re-balanced the difficulty levels that are available in the demo and made a few other UI tweaks here and there that should make things a little nicer to play. The game will now be [i]slightly[/i] harder on easy and normal, and, well, [i]much[/i] harder on harder difficulties. Which is why they're hard!

So that makes sense.

I've also translated both the pre-release main game and the demo into four new languages:

[list]
[*] German
[*] French
[*] Japanese
[*] Chinese
[/list]

Keep that feedback coming (Bluesky or Steam Discussions is best!) and let's work out all the Bugs & Tiles we can, together. And if you'd be willing to help me translate the game into a language that's not on the list above let me know; I'm looking to get the game into more European languages in particular, and I need your help!

notes.title: Isles & Tiles at WX Games Weekend in Yorkshire
notes.content:
We took [i]Isles & Tiles[/i] out for its first public showing this past weekend, at Game Republic's [url=https://gamerepublic.net/featured-events/wx-games-weekend/]WX Games Weekend[/url] in Wakefield. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45530603/7a73a4b068f47f5a84b15e1c883fc1b16875002d.jpg[/img]

Apparently there were around 6000 people who visited over a two-day event, and we were delighted to have hundreds of folks play through the first scenario of [i]Isles & Tiles[/i]. Heard lots of great feedback, made a bunch of new friends, and we certainly had a blast watching folks play the game and get into the nitty-gritty of buildings decks and designing islands!

We're particularly pleased with the super-chill soundtrack we've put together, but a big gaming convention isn't exactly the best place to enjoy a bit of relaxed ambient folk music. So instead we brought along our harpist -- one half of the harp/clarinet duo that's recorded every track -- and let people try out the game with a live-accompanied soundtrack. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45530603/105f08819394197a74fa02fd811530ffc7db16da.jpg[/img]

You can get a sneak peek at that soundtrack by checking out the first teaser trailer, which shows off just the harp part of one track. We're keeping the clarinet under wraps until the demo comes out, but trust us -- it's gonna be gold.
